New Environment Setup Guide ​

A step-by-step runbook for spinning up a new Firebase environment (e.g. staging or production) for the Sanjeev AI platform. Based on lessons learned from configuring sanjeev-ai-staging.

1. Prerequisites ​

  • [ ] Firebase CLI installed: npx -y firebase-tools@latest --version
  • [ ] gcloud CLI installed and authenticated: gcloud auth login
  • [ ] Node.js 20+ installed (check with node -v)
  • [ ] Java 21+ installed (required by Firebase Emulator): java -version
  • [ ] A new Firebase/GCP project created at console.firebase.google.com

2. GCP — Enable Required APIs ​

Run this single command to enable all APIs used by the platform:

powershell
gcloud services enable `
  aiplatform.googleapis.com `
  texttospeech.googleapis.com `
  youtube.googleapis.com `
  storage.googleapis.com `
  firestore.googleapis.com `
  cloudfunctions.googleapis.com `
  artifactregistry.googleapis.com `
  cloudbuild.googleapis.com `
  run.googleapis.com `
  eventarc.googleapis.com `
  cloudbilling.googleapis.com `
  cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com `
  logging.googleapis.com `
  pubsub.googleapis.com `
  --project=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

⚠️ After enabling APIs, wait 2–3 minutes before testing — propagation takes time.

3. GCP — Create a Local Dev Service Account ​

The Firebase emulator runs with a fake service account that cannot sign URLs or call production APIs. You need a real service account for local development.

3a. Create the service account ​

powershell
gcloud iam service-accounts create antigravity-access `
  --display-name="Antigravity Local Dev" `
  --project=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

3b. Grant required roles ​

powershell
# Vertex AI (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Imagen 4, Veo)
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding <YOUR_PROJECT_ID> `
  --member="serviceAccount:antigravity-access@<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>.iam.gserviceaccount.com" `
  --role="roles/aiplatform.user"

# Editor covers Text-to-Speech, Storage, YouTube, and all other APIs
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding <YOUR_PROJECT_ID> `
  --member="serviceAccount:antigravity-access@<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>.iam.gserviceaccount.com" `
  --role="roles/editor"

3c. Download the key ​

In the GCP Console → IAM → Service Accounts:

  1. Click on antigravity-access@<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>
  2. Go to Keys → Add Key → JSON
  3. Save as functions/service-account.json

⚠️ This file is already in .gitignore. Never commit it.

4. Firebase — Project Configuration ​

4a. Set the active Firebase project ​

powershell
npx -y firebase-tools@latest use <YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

4b. Verify firebase.json targets ​

Make sure firebase.json references your new project ID where needed (hosting, functions, etc.).

4c. Configure frontend environment variables ​

Create frontend/.env.<environment> (e.g. .env.staging):

env
VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY=...
VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>.firebaseapp.com
VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>
VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>.firebasestorage.app
VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID=...
VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID=...

4d. Configure function secrets ​

Create functions/.secret.local for the emulator:

env
GEMINI_API_KEY=<YOUR_KEY>
YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID=<YOUR_KEY>
YOUTUBE_CLIENT_SECRET=<YOUR_KEY>

⚠️ This file must never be committed. It is already excluded via *.local in .gitignore.

5. Install Dependencies ​

powershell
# Frontend
cd frontend
npm install

# Functions
cd ../functions
npm install

6. Build Functions ​

The emulator loads from lib/ (compiled output), not src/. Always build before starting:

powershell
cd functions
npm run build

7. Start Local Development ​

Run these in separate terminal windows:

Terminal 1 — Frontend (Vite dev server):

powershell
cd frontend
npm run dev

Terminal 2 — Firebase Emulators (with real service account for signed URLs + API calls):

powershell
$env:GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="C:\<path-to-repo>\functions\service-account.json"
npx -y firebase-tools@latest emulators:start --only auth,firestore,functions,storage

💡 The GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS env var is required because:

  • The Firebase emulator uses a fake service account that has no client_email
  • Without it, getSignedUrl() and all production Google API calls will fail with PERMISSION_DENIED

8. Known Gotchas & Pitfalls ​

IssueCauseFix
Cannot find ffprobefluent-ffmpeg's mergeToFile() calls ffprobe internally; path not setffmpeg.setFfprobePath(ffprobeStatic.path) in generator.ts
Cannot sign data without client_emailEmulator fake SA has no credentialsSet GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS to real service account JSON
aiplatform.googleapis.com not enabledNew project doesn't have Vertex AI enabled by defaultRun gcloud services enable aiplatform.googleapis.com
PERMISSION_DENIED on Vertex AISA doesn't have roles/aiplatform.userGrant role via gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding
texttospeech.googleapis.com not enabledNew project doesn't have TTS enabledRun gcloud services enable texttospeech.googleapis.com
npm run dev not found in functions/dev script only exists in frontend/package.jsonRun npm run dev from frontend/ directory
Emulator uses wrong projectGCLOUD_PROJECT env var picks up active gcloud projectRun firebase use <project-id> before starting emulators
API propagation delayAPIs enabled but still 403 for 1–2 minutesWait 2–3 minutes after enabling an API before retrying
Permission 'iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob' deniedCloud Function service account cannot generate signed audio/video URLsGrant roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to the Compute Engine and App Engine service accounts (Step 12)
FAILED_PRECONDITION: The query requires an indexMulti-field queries on subcollections (like workflows) lack composite indexesDefine index in firestore.indexes.json and run firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes (Step 13)
TS5103: Invalid value for ignoreDeprecationsOutdated tsconfig options on modern TypeScriptSet "module": "node16", "moduleResolution": "node16" and remove deprecated fields in tsconfig.json
CI/CD ESLint failuresOverly strict formatting rules (e.g. line lengths, jsdoc) blocking buildsRelax ESLint rules in functions/.eslintrc.js by setting rules like "max-len": "off" and "valid-jsdoc": "off"
Permissions denied enabling artifactregistry.googleapis.comCI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions) lacks the serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin role to auto-enable backend APIs for Gen 2 functions on first deploy.Run gcloud services enable artifactregistry.googleapis.com cloudbuild.googleapis.com run.googleapis.com eventarc.googleapis.com manually.

9. Deploying to the New Environment ​

powershell
# Deploy Storage rules only
firebase deploy --only storage --project=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

# Deploy Firestore indexes only
firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes --project=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

# Deploy Firestore rules only
firebase deploy --only firestore:rules --project=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

# Deploy functions only
cd functions
firebase deploy --only functions --project=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

# Deploy frontend only (staging mode)
cd frontend
npm run build:staging
firebase deploy --only hosting --project=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

# Deploy everything
firebase deploy --project=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

10. CI/CD Pipeline Setup (GitHub Actions) ​

To enable automatic continuous integration and deployment when merging to staging or main (production), you must set up the correct IAM permissions and secrets:

10a. Configure GitHub Repository Secrets ​

Add the following secret in GitHub Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions:

  • FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_<ENVIRONMENT> (e.g. FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SANJEEV_AI_STAGING): The JSON key of your deployment service account.

10b. Mandatory Service Account IAM Roles ​

The deployment service account (used in the pipeline) must have the following roles on the Google Cloud / Firebase project:

  1. roles/cloudfunctions.developer (Deploy Cloud Functions)
  2. roles/iam.serviceAccountUser (Run functions under the default runtime identity)
  3. roles/firebasehosting.admin (Deploy Frontend Assets to Hosting)
  4. roles/firebaseauth.admin (Manage auth settings and authorized domains)
  5. roles/firebaserules.admin (CRITICAL: Allows compiling and deploying Firestore Security Rules. Without this, the pipeline fails silently during firestore deploy!).
  6. roles/datastore.owner (Allows the Firebase CLI to retrieve database metadata and deploy composite indexes).
  7. roles/secretmanager.admin (Allows the Firebase CLI to verify and bind Secret Manager secrets to Cloud Functions).

11. Cloud Function Runtime IAM Permissions (Signed URLs) ​

If Cloud Functions in your environment throw Permission 'iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob' denied when attempting to generate Voiceover Audio or Videos, you must authorize their execution identity.

11a. Identify the Runtime Service Accounts ​

  1. Compute Engine Default Service Account: PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com (Gen 2 Cloud Functions default identity)
  2. App Engine Default Service Account: PROJECT_ID@appspot.gserviceaccount.com

11b. Grant Service Account Token Creator Role ​

Run these commands to grant the Service Account Token Creator role:

powershell
# Grant to Compute Engine SA
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding <YOUR_PROJECT_ID> `
  --member="serviceAccount:<PROJECT_NUMBER>-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com" `
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"

# Grant to App Engine SA
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding <YOUR_PROJECT_ID> `
  --member="serviceAccount:<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>@appspot.gserviceaccount.com" `
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"

11c. Eventarc & Pub/Sub Propagation Roles ​

When you enable the Eventarc and Pub/Sub APIs for the first time, Google Cloud takes up to 5 minutes to automatically bind permissions to their internal service agents. To avoid CI/CD failing during this wait period, manually grant them:

powershell
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding <YOUR_PROJECT_ID> `
  --member="serviceAccount:service-<PROJECT_NUMBER>@gcp-sa-pubsub.iam.gserviceaccount.com" `
  --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"

gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding <YOUR_PROJECT_ID> `
  --member="serviceAccount:<PROJECT_NUMBER>-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com" `
  --role="roles/run.invoker"

gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding <YOUR_PROJECT_ID> `
  --member="serviceAccount:<PROJECT_NUMBER>-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com" `
  --role="roles/eventarc.eventReceiver"

12. Firestore Composite Index Setup ​

Any subcollection query that filters by field equality and orders by another field (such as our orchestrator workflow querying workflows by scriptId and ordering by createdAt DESC) requires a composite index. Without it, the background orchestrator function will crash.

12a. Define the workflows Index in firestore.indexes.json ​

Ensure your index file has the following entry:

json
{
  "indexes": [
    {
      "collectionGroup": "workflows",
      "queryScope": "COLLECTION",
      "fields": [
        { "fieldPath": "scriptId", "order": "ASCENDING" },
        { "fieldPath": "createdAt", "order": "DESCENDING" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "fieldOverrides": []
}

12b. Deploy the Index ​

Always run index deploys first before starting workflows:

powershell
firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes --project=<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>

13. Google Cloud Storage CORS Setup ​

By default, Firebase/GCP Storage buckets block cross-origin requests from web applications (including local dev servers like http://localhost:5173 and deployed web hosting). This results in console errors such as: Access to image/audio at '...' from origin '...' has been blocked by CORS policy.

13a. Create cors.json file ​

Create a temporary cors.json configuration file:

json
[
  {
    "origin": ["*"],
    "method": ["GET"],
    "maxAgeSeconds": 3600
  }
]

13b. Apply the CORS configuration using gcloud ​

Execute the following command to update your storage bucket's CORS policy:

powershell
gcloud storage buckets update gs://<YOUR_PROJECT_ID>.firebasestorage.app --cors-file=cors.json

14. Checklist Summary ​

  • [ ] GCP project created
  • [ ] All APIs enabled (Step 2)
  • [ ] Dev service account created with correct roles (Step 3)
  • [ ] service-account.json downloaded to functions/ and gitignored (Step 3c)
  • [ ] functions/.secret.local configured with API keys (Step 4d)
  • [ ] frontend/.env.<environment> configured with Firebase config (Step 4c)
  • [ ] npm install run in both frontend/ and functions/
  • [ ] npm run build run in functions/
  • [ ] Emulators started with GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS set (Step 7)
  • [ ] GitHub Action Service Account granted all 5 mandatory deploy roles (Step 10b)
  • [ ] Cloud Function Service Accounts granted roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator (Step 11b)
  • [ ] Firestore Composite Indexes deployed successfully (Step 12b)
  • [ ] GCS Storage CORS Config applied successfully (Step 13b)
  • [ ] Storage Security Rules deployed successfully (Step 9)
  • [ ] Firestore Security Rules deployed successfully (Step 9)
  • [ ] Frontend dev server started from frontend/ directory
